theory.overview: Bloom Filter is a space-efficient probabilistic data structure for set membership testing. Uses bit array and multiple hash functions. Can return false positives (says element exists when it doesn't) but never false negatives. Used in databases, caches, spell checkers, and network systems. This chapter covers Bloom filter structure, operations, false positive analysis, and applications.

sections.title: Bloom Filter Structure
sections.content: Bit array of size m. k hash functions map elements to k positions in array. To add element: set bits at all k hash positions. To query: check if all k bits are set. If any bit is 0, element definitely not in set. If all bits are 1, element probably in set (possible false positive).

sections.title: Operations
sections.content: Add(x): compute k hash values, set bits at those positions. Time: $O(k)$. Query(x): compute k hash values, check if all bits set. Time: $O(k)$. No deletion operation (standard Bloom filter). Counting Bloom Filter variant supports deletion using counters instead of bits.

sections.title: False Positive Rate
sections.content: Probability of false positive depends on m (size), k (hash functions), n (elements inserted). Formula: $p \approx (1 - e^{-kn/m})^k$. Optimal k: $k = (m/n) \ln 2$. For 1% false positive with n elements, need $m \approx 9.6n$ bits and $k \approx 7$ hash functions.

sections.title: Hash Functions
sections.content: Need k independent hash functions. Can use: different seeds for same hash function, or different hash functions (Murmur, FNV, etc.). Hash functions should be fast and uniformly distributed. Poor hash functions increase false positive rate.

sections.title: Bloom Filter vs Hash Set
sections.content: Bloom Filter: space-efficient, no false negatives, has false positives, no deletion (standard). Hash Set: more space, exact membership, supports deletion. Choose Bloom Filter when space is critical and false positives acceptable.

keyConcepts.name: False Positive
keyConcepts.description: Query returns true for element not in set. Probability depends on m, k, n. Never false negatives.

keyConcepts.name: Hash Functions
keyConcepts.description: k independent hash functions map element to k positions. More hash functions reduce false positives but increase computation.
keyConcepts.tradeoff: More k → lower false positive, slower operations

keyConcepts.name: Bit Array
keyConcepts.description: Compact representation using bits. Each bit represents whether hash position has been set.

keyConcepts.name: Counting Bloom Filter
keyConcepts.description: Variant using counters instead of bits. Supports deletion by decrementing counters. Uses more space.

steps.title: Initialize
steps.description: Create bit array of size m, initialize to 0. Choose k hash functions.

steps.title: Add Element
steps.description: Compute k hash values, set bits at those positions.
steps.code: for i in range(k): pos = hash_functions[i](element) % m; bit_array[pos] = 1;

steps.title: Query Element
steps.description: Compute k hash values, check if all bits are set.
steps.code: for i in range(k): pos = hash_functions[i](element) % m; if bit_array[pos] == 0: return False; return True;

steps.title: Interpret Result
steps.description: False = definitely not in set. True = probably in set (possible false positive).
steps.code: if result == False: definitely not; else: probably in set;

steps.title: Calculate False Positive Rate
steps.description: Calculate probability of false positive based on m, k, n.

snippets.title: Bloom Filter Implementation
False Positive Rate
snippets.code:
import math

def false_positive_rate(m, k, n):
    """Calculate false positive rate"""
    return (1 - math.exp(-k * n / m)) ** k

# Example: m=1000 bits, k=3 hashes, n=100 elements
p = false_positive_rate(1000, 3, 100)
print(f"False positive rate: {p:.4f}")

snippets.title: Optimal Parameters
snippets.code:
import math

def optimal_parameters(n, target_p):
    """Calculate optimal m and k for target false positive rate"""
    m = -n * math.log(target_p) / (math.log(2) ** 2)
    k = (m / n) * math.log(2)
    return int(m), int(k)

# Example: n=1000 elements, target p=0.01 (1%)
m, k = optimal_parameters(1000, 0.01)
print(f"Optimal size: {m} bits, Optimal k: {k}")
